- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, reduce forecast for next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction.  
- If forecast consistently undershoots true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, apply upward bias correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.5+), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing out extreme swings.  
- If recent sentiment is trending upward but forecast is declining, reverse the trend direction in next 2–3 days.  
- If forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment strength.  
- If forecast is <10% below true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, apply upward correction proportional to sentiment strength.
